name: Tabimorelin
lead: Tabimorelin (NN703) is an experimental, orally active growth hormone secretagogue that was among the earlier compounds in its class. It acts on the ghrelin receptor to stimulate growth hormone release.[1][2]

Published human studies are early-phase work in healthy men, an interaction study with the CYP3A4 substrate midazolam, and work in growth hormone-deficient adults.[3][4][5][6] It is not approved for any use. No studies have tested it for appearance purposes.

paras: Tabimorelin is a potent agonist of the ghrelin receptor. It produced sustained rises in growth hormone and IGF-1 and smaller, temporary rises in ACTH, cortisol and prolactin.[1][3][4] It was found to be a mechanism-based inhibitor of CYP3A4, which could cause drug interactions.[1][5]

A single-dose, double-blind placebo-controlled study in healthy men escalated across eight dose levels and found it well tolerated, with higher growth hormone exposure than placebo at several doses.[3] A 7-day once-daily study in healthy men found dose-related increases in growth hormone.[4] A study of its interaction with midazolam examined the effect of its CYP3A4 inhibition in 17 men.[5] Wikipedia notes that clinical benefit in adults with growth hormone deficiency was limited, mainly in the most severely deficient.[1]

Analytical chemists have developed methods to detect tabimorelin, capromorelin and macimorelin metabolites in urine and plasma for sports doping control.[2] In rats lacking leptin signalling, its adipogenic and orexigenic effects were reduced.[6]

card.summary: Early experimental oral GH secretagogue; a few early human studies and no appearance data.
card.note: Experimental only; inhibits CYP3A4, so drug interactions are possible.

quick.overview:
Tabimorelin is an experimental oral drug from the first generation of growth hormone secretagogues. It was tested in healthy men and in adults with growth hormone deficiency.

It raised growth hormone and IGF-1, but clinical benefit was limited and it was never approved.
quick.mechanism: It mimics ghrelin at the GH secretagogue receptor to trigger growth hormone release.
quick.risks: It inhibits the liver enzyme CYP3A4, creating potential interactions with other drugs. Human data are limited to a few early studies.
